changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For product leaders replacing a homegrown billing system: Stop billing being a tax on the roadmap. Change a price, add a trial or set up proration in a few clicks, not a quarter of engineering work.
changes.why: Owen rejected the revenue framing outright ("we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap."), while the price-change demo drew "that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes."

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: In late-stage deals, lead with a payback number built with the champion from their own inputs: engineering time spent on pricing changes, billing errors, and subscriptions that lapse on failed cards. Use the independent study only as supporting proof behind that number.
changes.why: Owen asked for payback, we sent the general ROI deck with the study, and he said "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours."

changes.change: For champions taking a homegrown billing replacement to the CFO: a cost-of-doing-nothing line that makes the status quo urgent, for example: Your homegrown billing costs you a quarter of engineering on every pricing change, plus revenue from subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it. Fill in the customer's own figures.
changes.why: Finance treated the project as "nice to have" under the rule "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded.", and Owen had named the costs (quarter-long pricing changes, lapsed subscriptions) but nobody added them up.

changes.change: For homegrown billing replacements, back migration claims with a reference call from a customer who has already moved existing subscriptions over, rather than a migration doc. Cover whether card details had to be re-collected and whether the move was staged.
changes.why: Owen's migration questions were about not asking landlords for card details again and moving in stages, and although we had a doc, he wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.
